title: Honey Grove, Texas, and the gospel music of his childhood church
summary: Price confirms he was born in Honey Grove, names nearby towns, and describes the hymns, a cappella songs, tambourines and triangle he first heard.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: You were born in Honey Grove, Texas?
Yeah, I was born in Honey Grove, Texas. That's a little - small town in the eastern part of Texas.
What was the nearest big place?

Greenville...Paris...you know, in the eastern area you had Greenville, Paris and, if you went far enough, you'd go to Denison, up on the Red River Valley. I mean, the Red River... north of Honey Grove.
What was the musical environment there...I mean, what was the first music you heard...at home, or...?

I came from a line of religious preachers and gospel singers. Quite naturally, the first songs I heard would be... well, the lullabies, of course, but then, right off the bat we started going to church, so we heard many of the gospel songs, and the church songs, and hymns and things of that sort. And occasionally, when we were big enough, go and go and we used to/visit...not inside the church, but, outside, and listen to the Church of God and Christ singing, they played you know, with tambourines and a peculiar thing/called, you know, the triangle. You know what a triangle is? They played the triangle in the church and...there were very few pianos, of course--some broken-down organs, and many of the songs were a capella, with sometimes a preacher leading, or, you know, that kind of thing, where
the preacher would start a song; he would say the words, and the members would repeat after him, and then build up into a climax / (laughter) like Henry Red Allen'
